posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: 7.50% GG 2056 Yield — Hello, G-Sec interest/coupon is taxable as “Income from Other Sources”. If you hold the G-Sec till maturity and receive the face value/principal , the principal repayment itself is generally not taxable. Capital gain may arise if you sell/transfer the G-Sec before maturity at a price different from its cost. Filing ITR-4 under presumptive taxation does not make G-Sec interest tax-free.
